newsitem.title: USA: Pulte venture to build 500 homes in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Pulte venture to build 500 homes in Mexico.

text.p: Expanding efforts to improve living conditions for Mexican "maquiladora" workers, Pulte Corp. said Wednesday it signed a deal to build about 500 homes for some of Sony Corp.'s workers in Mexico.

The homes will be built mainly in Nuevo Laredo, Mexico, by Condak-Pulte, a joint venture between Pulte and Grupo Condak, a developer based in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico. The modest dwellings will house employees of Sony Magneticos de Mexico S.A. de C.V., which produces cassette tape products and computer floppy disks.
The project is similar to another deal Condak-Pulte signed with General Motors Corp. in June to build about 6,000 new subsidised homes for employees of the automaker's Delphi Automotive Systems unit.
Scott Campbell, a spokesman for Pulte, one of the largest U.S. homebuilders, said the two deals will use very similar financing arrangments.

Both GM and Sony will provide qualified workers with down payment assistance on mortgages to be provided by Mexico's housing authority, the Instituto del Fondo Nacional de la Vivienda para los Trabajadores.
"We looked at the GM deal as a template for our company," Campbell said, adding that the GM project will likely be expanded to 7,000 homes.

The financing programmes are aimed at improving poor living conditions for workers in maquiladora industries located near the U.S. border. The homes, made of concrete with 400 to 600 square feet of living space, will sell for $10,000 to $12,000 with full utilities.
Campbell said Pulte does not expect to begin closing sales of the homes until mid-1998, which will allow Sony workers time to save for the down payments. Sony Magneticos employs about 2,600 people.
